body:
Supersedes #28381, fixes #28372 in a simpler way.

The PEG transformer merged `(A UNION B) UNION C` into one N-ary UNION node, so the inner set operation never resolved its own result type and `87::INTEGER` was cast straight to `VARCHAR` instead of through `DOUBLE`.

`TransformSelectSetOpChain` now only merges into the N-ary nodes it builds itself. A chain's first operand can only be a set operation when it was written in parentheses (no other
`SelectAtom` alternative produces one), so such an operand stays nested and the binder stages the cast through it. Unparenthesized chains are unchanged and still become a single N-ary node.

linked_issues.body:
### What happens?


In DuckDB v1.5.6, a parenthesized inner `UNION` resolves `DOUBLE` and `INTEGER` to `DOUBLE` when evaluated on its own. However, when this inner query is followed by an outer `UNION` with a `VARCHAR` branch, the integer appears to be converted directly to `VARCHAR`, bypassing the intermediate `DOUBLE` conversion.

Changing only the outer operator to `UNION ALL` changes the value from `'87'` to `'87.0'`. Introducing a derived-table boundary also changes the result. The discrepancy can affect duplicate elimination and therefore result cardinality.

The reproducer requires no tables, extensions, external files, or project-specific code.


## Expected behavior

The explicitly grouped inner query has output type `DOUBLE`. Its `87::INTEGER` branch should therefore produce `87.0` before the outer operation converts that value to `VARCHAR`.

Under that interpretation, Queries A, B, and C should all return the same three strings: `'1.5'`, `'87.0'`, and `'text'`. There are no duplicate values in these results, so changing the outer `UNION` to `UNION ALL` should not change either values or cardinality.

If binding types across adjacent UNION nodes as a single operation is intentional, could you clarify why explicit parenthesization does not preserve the inner conversion, and why changing the outer duplicate-handling mode changes the value?


### To Reproduce

```sql
-- The inner query resolves to DOUBLE.
DESCRIBE (SELECT 1.5::DOUBLE AS x UNION SELECT 87::INTEGER);
-- x DOUBLE

SELECT 1.5::DOUBLE AS x UNION SELECT 87::INTEGER;
-- 1.5, 87.0

-- Query A
(SELECT 1.5::DOUBLE AS x UNION SELECT 87::INTEGER)
UNION SELECT 'text'::VARCHAR;
-- Actual: '1.5', '87', 'text'

-- Query B: only the outer operator changes.
(SELECT 1.5::DOUBLE AS x UNION SELECT 87::INTEGER)
UNION ALL SELECT 'text'::VARCHAR;
-- Actual: '1.5', '87.0', 'text'

-- Query C: preserve the inner result through a derived table.
SELECT x
FROM (SELECT 1.5::DOUBLE AS x UNION SELECT 87::INTEGER) q
UNION SELECT 'text'::VARCHAR;
-- Actual: '1.5', '87.0', 'text'
```
